requirement:
An item with no attachments has an empty list. A language may return empty
lists for every item.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.empty` has two clauses. The first is "An item with no attachments has an empty list." The second is "A language may return empty lists for every item." Both describe observable results only. The first clause names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. An implementation could build the empty list at one site or at many, or hold it in any container. A different structure would still return an empty list for an item with no attachments, so the structure is discretionary. The second clause is a MAY. It imposes nothing to check. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, so having no implementation roots is not a gap. Whether an empty list is actually returned is a behavioral matter. I left it to the behavioral criterion. behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation: an item with no attachments has an empty list. It also says a language may return empty lists for every item, which is permission only (MAY) and needs no test. Two tests cover the obligation, and both carry `{test}` markers for it. - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` builds an `OutlineItem::new(...)` with no attachments and asserts `item.attachments.is_empty()`. This checks the default empty list directly. - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` parses real sources for each bundled language and collects every attachment from every item. It asserts the exact expected `(kind, text)` list. - The `test.txt` case expects no attachments at all, so the plain-text language returns empty lists. - The markdown, TypeScript, YAML, TOML and Python cases include text that looks like an attachment but isn't, such as `# literal`, `// string`, `
html
` and ``. The exact comparison rejects any spurious attachment on an item that should have none. Because the attachment list is a `Vec`, "no attachments" can only be shown as an empty list. These assertions rule out spurious entries, so I found no gap.
